title: Four ways to own gold, and the new one JPMorgan and HSBC just tested in London
body: The pilot changes how gold is held and moved, not how much investors want, so it has little bearing on prices near term. Spot gold remains under pressure from near-certain expectations of a December Fed hike and sits not far above last week's more-than-one-year low. The longer-term effect could be supportive. Gold that can be pledged as collateral in real time earns a role on institutional balance sheets beyond being a store of value. For crypto, the pilot adds institutional competition to on-chain gold tokens such as XAUT and PAXG. It also gives regulators a working wholesale model to point to as the FCA shapes its rules for tokenised gold. --- Earlier: How crypto loans unwind: what a $43.8 million ether sale teaches about leverage --- Gold has always been trusted and hard to move; London's biggest dealers have now tested a way to keep the trust and lose some of the weight. Summary: The World Gold Council said on November 24 that JPMorgan, HSBC and StoneX had completed the first live, legally binding trades using Pooled Gold Interests (PGIs). The firms traded, settled and used fractional ownership of physical bars as collateral, with no metal leaving the vault. ICE Benchmark Administration operates the system and Baton Systems provides the settlement technology. The WGC release doesn't say it runs on a blockchain. PGIs aim to combine the legal ownership of allocated gold with the flexibility of unallocated gold.

title: PBOC is expected to set the USD/CNY reference rate at 6.6559 – Reuters estimate
body: The People's Bank of China is due to set the daily USD/CNY reference rate at around 0115 GMT (2115 US Eastern time), a fixing that remains one of the most closely watched signals in Asian foreign exchange markets. China operates a managed floating exchange rate system, under which the renminbi (yuan) is allowed to trade within a prescribed band around a central reference rate, or midpoint, set each trading day by the PBOC. The current trading band permits the currency to move plus or minus 2% from the official midpoint during onshore trading hours. Each morning, the PBOC determines the midpoint based on a range of inputs. These include the previous day's closing price, movements in major currencies, particularly the US dollar, broader international FX conditions, and domestic economic considerations such as capital flows, growth momentum and financial stability objectives. The midpoint is not a purely mechanical calculation, allowing policymakers discretion to guide market expectations. Once the midpoint is announced, onshore USD/CNY is free to trade within the allowable band. If market pressures push the yuan toward either edge of that range, the central bank may step in to smooth volatility. Intervention can take the form of direct buying or selling of yuan, adjustments to liquidity conditions, or guidance through state-owned banks. As a result, the daily fixing is often interpreted as a policy signal rather than just a technical reference point.

title: How crypto loans unwind: what a $43.8 million ether sale teaches about leverage
body: BTCS's sale is too small to move ether's price directly. The bigger effect is on how investors view listed crypto treasury firms, whose shares tend to trade as leveraged bets on the coins they hold. BTCS fell nearly 9%. The episode may push investors to look harder at how much other ether-heavy companies have borrowed. Spot ether ETFs are in a run of outflows and bitcoin is below $60,000, so risk appetite across crypto is fragile. Further forced-sale disclosures could hurt sentiment more than they add to supply. - A balance sheet that looked well covered on paper was only a 19% ether drop from forced liquidation, and BTCS paid to close that gap before Aave closed it for them. Summary: BTCS sold about 27,300 ETH on November 20 for $43.8 million and used it all to repay Aave debt, per an 8-K filed November 23. Its Aave borrowing fell to about $10.5 million from an implied $54.3 million. Its November 9 position (about $64.1 million owed against 46,676 ETH) implied a liquidation price of around $1,720. Ether fell near $1,560 on November 20. The company is left with about 24,245 ETH. TheStreet puts its loan-to-value ratio at about 32%. Its DeFi unit, Imperium, has paused its liquidity pool positions, and about $17.9 million of convertible notes are due in 2027. Nasdaq-listed BTCS sold about 27,300 ETH on November 20 and used the full $43.8 million in proceeds to repay debt on Aave, the decentralised lending protocol, according to a Form 8-K filed with the SEC on November 23.

title: Saudi Arabia triples its oil storage in Japan as Tokyo buys 8m barrels to refill reserves

For Saudi Arabia, extra storage in Japan gives it barrels positioned close to Asian buyers, which helps it respond quickly to disruptions and defend market share as Gulf flows recover. If other importers strike similar arrangements, as MUFG expects, the trend would support Middle Eastern exporters' long-term grip on Asian demand. -- Japan is restocking its emergency reserves with Saudi crude and giving Riyadh three times more room to store oil on Japanese soil, a sign that this year's Gulf disruptions are pushing buyers and sellers toward deeper supply partnerships.

title: Australia's Core Inflation Eases as Weighted Mean CPI Slows to 3.4% in October
body: Australia's underlying inflation pressures moderated in October 2026, with the weighted mean Consumer Price Index (CPI) easing to 3.4% year-over-year, down from 3.6% recorded in the third quarter of 2026. The data, updated on 25 November 2026, point to a gradual cooling in core price growth as measured on an annual basis. The weighted mean CPI is a key gauge of underlying inflation, stripping out some of the most volatile price movements to provide a clearer view of persistent price trends. In this case, the "actual" figure compares price changes in October 2026 with October 2025, while the "previous" reading reflects the change in the third quarter of 2026 versus the same quarter a year earlier. The slight deceleration from 3.6% to 3.4% suggests that inflationary pressures remain present but are slowly easing, a development likely to be closely watched by policymakers and financial markets assessing the trajectory of Australia's inflation and potential implications for monetary policy.
